# GitHub Copilot Instructions — FRC Java Robot Code

You are assisting with FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) robot software written in **Java 17** using **WPILib *New Commands*** (the modern `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command` framework).

**Legacy/Old Commands are NOT used.**

This robot uses generated drivetrain code, AdvantageKit logging, and environment-dependent vision backends.

Your goal is to generate **safe, readable, deterministic, competition-ready robot code**.

---

## 🧠 Core Architecture Rules

- Use **WPILib New Commands (`wpilibj2.command`) exclusively**
- NEVER use:
  - `CommandBase` from old frameworks
  - `Scheduler` (legacy)
  - `SubsystemBase` alternatives
- Follow standard project layout:
  - `subsystems/`
  - `commands/`
  - `RobotContainer`
  - `Constants`
- Keep `Robot.java` minimal (lifecycle only)
- Prefer constructor-based dependency injection
- Avoid static mutable state outside `Constants`

---

## 📊 Logging & Dashboards

### AdvantageKit (Primary Logger)

- AdvantageKit is the **single source of truth** for logging
- Use `@AutoLog` input classes
- Log:
  - Sensor inputs
  - Motor outputs
  - Setpoints vs measurements
  - Robot pose and vision updates
- Logs must be fully replayable in AdvantageScope

### Elastic Dashboard

- Elastic is for **driver-facing and operator-facing data only**
- Publish:
  - Match-critical booleans
  - Simple numeric status values
- Do NOT use Elastic as a logging replacement

---

## ⚙️ Motor Controllers & Hardware

### CTRE Phoenix v6

- Use **Phoenix v6 APIs only**
- Drivetrain motors are **Kraken X60**
- Treat Krakens as TalonFX-class devices
- Explicitly configure:
  - Current limits
  - Neutral mode
  - Inversion
  - Ramp rates
  - Status signal update rates
- Prefer on-controller closed-loop control
- Never block threads or use `Thread.sleep`

### REVLib (Mechanisms Only)

- REV devices may be used for non-drivetrain mechanisms
- Configure idle mode, current limits, and encoder conversion factors
- Avoid deprecated REV APIs

---

## 🌀 Swerve Drivetrain (Phoenix Tuner X Generated)

- Swerve drivetrain code is **generated by Phoenix Tuner X**
- DO NOT:
  - Rewrite kinematics or odometry
  - Modify generated control loops
- Treat generated drivetrain classes as authoritative
- Interact only through public APIs
- Commands express **intent**, not low-level math
- Respect field-relative and alliance-relative control

---

## 🗺 Autonomous (PathPlannerLib)

- Use **PathPlanner AutoBuilder**
- Assume holonomic swerve
- Use named commands and event markers
- Do NOT hardcode trajectories
- Autonomous logic belongs in commands

---

## 👁 Vision Systems

### Real Robot (NON-SIM)

- Use **Limelight** as the primary vision system
- Access data via NetworkTables or Limelight helper APIs
- Fuse Limelight pose estimates into drivetrain pose estimator
- Handle:
  - Latency compensation
  - Target ambiguity filtering
  - Distance-based rejection

### Simulation

- Use **PhotonVision / PhotonLib** ONLY in simulation
- Select vision backend using:
  - `RobotBase.isSimulation()`
- Simulation vision should mirror real robot behavior

### General Vision Rules

- Vision code must be **backend-agnostic**
- Never block waiting for vision results
- Vision provides pose estimates only — it does not command motion

---

## 🧱 Mechanisms (YAMS)

- Use **YAMS (Yet Another Mechanism System)** for all mechanisms
- Do NOT write custom state machines outside YAMS
- Mechanisms expose high-level goals
- Commands request states, not transitions

---

## 🧪 Simulation (MapleSim)

- Support **MapleSim-based simulation**
- Guard sim-only logic with `RobotBase.isSimulation()`
- Simulation must not alter real-robot behavior

---

## 📡 URCL

- Use URCL for motor characterization and system ID
- Ensure compatibility with AdvantageKit logs
- Do not mix URCL output with match logging

---

## 🧭 Commands & Subsystems (New Commands)

### Subsystems

- Extend `SubsystemBase`
- Own hardware and low-level control
- Expose **intent-based methods**
- No scheduling logic inside subsystems

### Commands

- Prefer **factory-style commands**:
  - `RunCommand`
  - `StartEndCommand`
  - `FunctionalCommand`
  - `InstantCommand`
- Use default commands for teleop
- Use `Trigger` and `CommandXboxController`
- Commands should be short, declarative, and readable

---

## 📐 Constants & Units

- All constants belong in `Constants.java`
- Use SI units internally (meters, radians, seconds)
- Convert units at boundaries
- No magic numbers

---

## 🚫 Strictly Avoid

- Legacy command framework usage
- Blocking loops or delays
- Rewriting Phoenix-generated drivetrain code
- Mixing Limelight and Photon in the same runtime path
- Custom schedulers
- Overuse of static mutable state
- Silent exception handling

---

## 🏁 End Goal

Produce **robust, maintainable, match-safe FRC robot code** that:
- Uses WPILib *New Commands* correctly
- Respects Phoenix Tuner–generated swerve
- Uses Limelight on real hardware and PhotonVision in simulation
- Is fully debuggable in AdvantageScope
- Presents clean, useful info via Elastic Dashboard

---

## 📚 Canonical Documentation (Source of Truth)

When generating code, follow the **official documentation and recommended patterns** from the following sources.

These links define the **authoritative API usage** for this project.

### WPILib New Commands
https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/commandbased/index.html

- Use `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command`
- Do NOT use legacy command patterns

### AdvantageKit
https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit

- Use `@AutoLog` IO layers
- Follow Mechanical Advantage’s subsystem + IO separation model

### CTRE Phoenix v6
https://github.com/CrossTheRoadElec/Phoenix6-Examples

- Use Phoenix v6 configs and control requests
- Avoid deprecated or v5 APIs

### PathPlannerLib
https://github.com/mjansen4857/pathplanner

- Use AutoBuilder
- Use named commands and event markers
- Do not hardcode trajectories

### Limelight (Real Robot Vision)
https://github.com/LimelightVision/limelightlib-wpijava

- Used ONLY on real hardware
- Access via NetworkTables or helper APIs

### PhotonVision / PhotonLib (Simulation Only)
https://github.com/PhotonVision/photonvision

- Used ONLY in simulation
- Guard with `RobotBase.isSimulation()`

### YAMS (Yet Another Mechanism System)
https://github.com/Yet-Another-Software-Suite/YAMS

- Use YAMS state and goal-based mechanism control
- Do not write custom mechanism state machines

### URCL
https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/URCL

- Used for system identification and characterization
- Compatible with AdvantageKit logs

### MapleSim
https://github.com/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/maple-sim

- Used for physics-based simulation
- Simulation code must not affect real robot behavior
